CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who injured his right knee one week ago at a trampoline park while jumping with his wife. He heard a snap and experienced instant pain. This was his first time visiting a trampoline park. The injury occurred during recreational activity, not as part of a formal exercise regimen. Patient reports pain on the lateral (outside) aspect of the right knee. He has taken acetaminophen for pain relief with minimal benefit. He has elevated the knee but has not tried ice or heat. He reports a slight limp and can bear weight on the affected leg, though with some difficulty. He denies regular exercise routine.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports pain with certain knee movements and a slight limp with ambulation.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension.
Diabetes mellitus.

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily (for hypertension; patient reports taking it most days).
Metformin 500 mg (for diabetes; patient reports taking it regularly).
Acetaminophen (taken for knee pain with minimal benefit).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient goes to the trampoline park infrequently. He does not have a consistent exercise regimen. Regarding diet, patient is trying to watch what he eats and is attempting to watch carbohydrates but is not counting calories or following a specific diet. He is not on a low-salt diet.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure elevated at 180/80 mmHg.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmur appreciated.
Lungs: Clear bilaterally.
Right knee: Tenderness to palpation on the lateral aspect; no tenderness on medial aspect. Patient able to bend and straighten knee with some limitation. Ecchymosis and edema noted along the lateral aspect. No effusion noted. Decent range of motion present. Patient has a slight limp with ambulation. Able to bear weight with difficulty.

RESULTS
Right knee X-ray: No evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right knee pain: Lateral ligament strain. Prescribed meloxicam 15 mg daily for pain and swelling. Referred to physical therapy for strengthening and injury prevention. Further imaging may be considered if pain persists. Injury expected to heal on its own.
2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Ordered echocardiogram due to concern about blood pressure control. Medication modification may be necessary.
3. Diabetes mellitus: Ordered hemoglobin A1c to assess long-term blood glucose control. Ordered lipid panel for possible medication adjustments.
